title: How Pompeii Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck explain the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE that buried Pompeii, Herculaneum, Stabiae and other towns around the Bay of Naples. They cover the town's wealthy resort culture, the volcano's stratovolcano structure and the Campanian arc subduction setting, the eruption timeline with Pliny the Younger's eyewitness letter, pyroclastic flows and pliny eruptions, the disputed date (August 24 versus October or November), and the town's rediscovery in the 1700s. They then discuss Giuseppe Fiorelli's plaster-cast method, CT scans of the casts showing head injuries and good teeth, the sexually explicit Roman art, damaging past excavation methods such as paraffin wax on frescoes, UNESCO's endangered listing, and the Great Pompeii Project. The episode ends with a listener mail about German monument removal and Nazi history.

segments.title: Tour dates and intro banter
segments.summary: Tour date announcements in Boston, DC, St. Louis, Cleveland and Denver, followed by casual banter about a Netflix documentary on National Lampoon and the hosts' plan to cover Pompeii.

segments.title: Vesuvius and the Bay of Naples setting
segments.summary: The hosts describe Vesuvius as a stratovolcano built up from past eruptions, explain subduction along the Campanian arc where the African and Eurasian plates meet, and describe Pompeii as a wealthy, cosmopolitan resort town with temples, theaters and farmland rich in volcanic soil.

segments.title: Pink Floyd and Pompeii's amphitheater
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Pink Floyd's Echoes performance in the Pompeii amphitheater and David Gilmour's 2016 concert there, and the region's fertile land and lemons.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief ad break before the eruption discussion.

segments.title: The eruption of 79 CE begins
segments.summary: The hosts describe the warning signs and lack of volcanic awareness among residents, previous earthquakes including one in 63 CE, and the buried earlier settlements. They discuss the timing of the eruption and the resources on the eruption.

segments.title: Pliny the Younger's account and pyroclastic flows
segments.summary: Pliny the Younger's firsthand account of darkness, ash fall and falling pumice at Misenum and Pompeii. Details of the Plinian eruption column, pyroclastic flows of ash and hot gas, and the tsunami-like sea retreat and the deaths of Pliny the Elder at Stabiae.
topics: Pliny the Elder death at Stabiae

segments.title: Disputed eruption date
segments.summary: Discussion of the traditional August 24 date from Pliny's letter, the alternative October or November evidence including harvested fruit and a coin, and the death toll and abandonment of the region.

segments.title: Rediscovery, plaster casts and modern research
segments.summary: The hosts cover the lost city's rediscovery in the 1700s under Charles III, Fiorelli's plaster-cast method, CT scans of casts revealing head injuries and good teeth, excavation damage such as paraffin wax on frescoes, UNESCO endangered listing, and the Great Pompeii Project.

segments.title: Listener mail on German monuments
segments.summary: A listener writes about Germany's approach to Nazi-era monuments and recommends the film Goodbye Lenin.
